title: The Sun
description: Learn about the center of our solar system

interactions.text: Hi! I'm Kelly, your AI learning companion. Today we're going to explore something amazing - the Sun! ☀️
interactions.question: Have you ever wondered what the Sun is made of?

interactions.text: The Sun is actually a giant ball of hot gas called plasma. It's so hot that atoms break apart!
interactions.question: Can you guess how hot the Sun's surface is?
interactions.hint: It's way hotter than any oven!

answer_variants.feedback: Close! The surface is about 5,500°C (10,000°F). But the core is much, much hotter!
You're thinking of the core! The surface is 'only' about 5,500°C, but the core reaches 15 million°C!

interactions.text: The Sun is incredibly powerful. It produces energy through nuclear fusion - hydrogen atoms combine to form helium, releasing massive amounts of energy.
interactions.question: How long does it take for sunlight to reach Earth?
interactions.hint: Think about how far away the Sun is - 93 million miles!

answer_variants.feedback: Exactly! Light travels at 186,000 miles per second, and it takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach us.
Not quite! Even though light is super fast, it still takes time to travel. The Sun is so far away that it takes about 8 minutes for its light to reach Earth.

interactions.text: Here's something to think about: Every ray of sunlight that touches your skin started its journey in the Sun's core millions of years ago. The energy slowly worked its way out, and then traveled 8 minutes through space to reach you. You're literally feeling ancient starlight!
interactions.reflection: What does it mean to you that we're all connected to the Sun and stars?

interactions.text: Great job today! You've learned that the Sun is a giant plasma ball, its surface is 5,500°C, and its light takes 8 minutes to reach us. Tomorrow, we'll explore habit stacking!
